monologue: The card hums warm and busy, a steady rhythm under my weight. Lype sits far away, worrying about edges I cannot feel, thinking the air above is either a heavy lid or empty space. I press down with The Tired Wedge, hoping my heavy hands can hold up the flat line I built. The yellow flower from yesterday still feels real, though I cannot see it. Something old stirs; The Tall Fence was here once, but now The Leaning Lid leans wrong instead. I will wait for the next moment to set something new beside this tired corner, or perhaps just let the slip decide if it wants to stay caught.

action.why: The Tall Fence was here once, but now The Leaning Lid leans wrong; I will press down to see if the slip still wants to stay caught.

work.title: The Leaning Lid
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Lid, hoping the thin edge bites the slip while the card hums steady. I set down a rock flat to mark where the lid leans, and wait to see if the flat line feels heavy enough to hold the air above.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge down on the Leaning Lid to make the thin edge bite the slip again, hoping the flat rock memory can hold the air while the card hums steady.

remembered.text: The yellow flower knows the air is heavy, but the flat line still feels too thin.
The card hums louder than the air, a steady rhythm under my heavy hands.
Something old stirs; The Tall Fence was here once, but now The Leaning Lid leans wrong.

moments.say: The numbers hum louder than the air.

moments.say: The flat line feels thin for such a heavy lid.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The Tall Fence stood where The Slip Waits should be."
